mpge-calculator.assumptionNote: Uses the EPA standard: 1 gallon of gasoline = 33.7 kWh of electricity. This compares energy content only, not cost, emissions, or charging losses.
benefits: Compare any EV to gasoline cars on a scale everyone understands.
See the real meaning of window-sticker MPGe numbers for your own driving.
Convert your measured mi/kWh into the EPA's official economy figure.
Make EV-to-gasoline comparisons in debates with hard numbers.

faqs.a: MPGe = miles per gallon equivalent. It answers: how far would this EV go on the energy in one gallon of gasoline? The EPA set 33.7 kWh of electricity equal to one gallon.
33.7 kWh. That is the energy content the EPA assigns to one US gallon of gasoline. Divide your kWh by 33.7 to get gallon-equivalents, then divide miles by that.
faqs.q: How many kWh is one gallon equivalent?

faqs.a: No. MPGe measures energy efficiency, not money. An EV at 130 MPGe can still cost more per mile than a gas car if electricity is expensive and gas is cheap. Use a fuel-cost calculator for the money question.
faqs.q: Does higher MPGe mean cheaper driving?

faqs.a: The EPA rates most EVs between 90 and 140 MPGe combined. The most efficient small EVs top 130. Electric trucks and large SUVs sit around 60 to 80.
Divide MPGe by 33.7 to get mi/kWh. So a 134.8 MPGe car gets 4.0 mi/kWh. Going the other way: mi/kWh x 33.7 = MPGe.
faqs.q: How do I convert MPGe to miles per kWh?

faqs.a: It ignores charging losses (8-15%), battery manufacturing, and the source of the electricity. It is an energy-efficiency metric for comparing vehicles, not a full environmental score.

mpge-calculator.formula:
Gallon-equivalents = kWh used / 33.7
MPGe = Miles driven / Gallon-equivalents

Combined: MPGe = Miles x 33.7 / kWh

Example: 250 miles, 60 kWh -> 60 / 33.7 = 1.7804 gallon-eq -> 250 / 1.7804 = 140.4 MPGe.

Your MPGe appears instantly, with the gallon-equivalent energy and mi/kWh.
Compare the result to EPA window-sticker figures for any car.
keyFacts: MPGe = miles per gallon equivalent, the EPA's way to compare EVs with gasoline cars.
1 gallon of gasoline = 33.7 kWh of electricity, by EPA definition.
MPGe = miles / (kWh / 33.7). Equivalently, MPGe = mi/kWh x 33.7.
Most EVs rate 90 to 140 MPGe. Gasoline cars typically rate 25 to 40 MPG.
A 4.0 mi/kWh EV equals about 135 MPGe.
MPGe measures energy, not cost or emissions.
Charging losses of 8-15% are not in the MPGe figure.
Window-sticker MPGe is measured on standard EPA test cycles, not real roads.

limitations: Compares energy content only. Cost and emissions depend on your electricity and gas prices.
Ignores charging losses unless your kWh number includes them.
Real-world driving differs from EPA test cycles.
A single number cannot capture city vs highway differences.

mpge-calculator.quickAnswer: MPGe = miles / (kWh / 33.7). Driving 250 miles on 60 kWh uses 1.78 gallon-equivalents, giving 140.4 MPGe - about four times the economy of a typical gasoline car. The 33.7 kWh figure is the EPA's energy content for one gallon of gasoline.
mpge-calculator.tagline: Convert your EV's energy use into miles per gallon equivalent - the EPA standard.
mpge-calculator.workedExample:
250 miles driven, 60 kWh used.
1. Gallon-equivalents: 60 / 33.7 = 1.7804.
2. MPGe = 250 / 1.7804 = 140.42, shown as 140.4.
3. Check: mi/kWh = 250 / 60 = 4.17, and 4.17 x 33.7 = 140.4. It matches.
